title: GPU mix regional price pulse + HC probe
summary: Exploratory sheet to quantify how GPU fleet mix and regional price moves interact with headcount phasing and pricing sensitivity. Focus: near-term 9-month burn, 18-month runway scenarios, and a conservative pricing shock case.
content:
Purpose and scope
- Quick probe for FY26-Q1 through FY27-Q2: measure sensitivity of unit economics to regional GPU price swings and planned hiring cadence.
- Not final budget. Working hypotheses for leadership discussion.

Context / motivation
- Infra costs have two moving pieces: spot-like burst capacity (third-party cloud GPU prices) and reserved/dedicated fleet (amortized, negotiated). Recent RFPs and partner feedback indicate H100 availability pressure in EMEA and APAC through Q2 2026.
- Product team expects embedding demand to grow ~3x from current baseline depending on GTM pushes. We need a matrix tying pricing changes to headcount ramp choices (SWE/infra/support) to keep gross margin above 60% for hosted API.

Key assumptions (baseline)
- Time horizon: 9 months (short) / 18 months (mid).
- Workloads: 60% generation (latency-sensitive), 30% embeddings, 10% evals/batch jobs.
- GPU units: baseline fleet mix = 55% A100-80GB equiv, 35% H100 equiv, 10% CPU/low-cost accelerators for evals.
- Effective per-token infra cost baseline: $0.000024/token (hosted mix weighted).
- Revenue per token (net of partner fees): $0.00012/token.
- Hiring plan (baseline nine months): +8 net FTEs: 3 infra, 2 backend SWE, 2 SRE, 1 customer-success engineer. Average fully-burdened cost per FTE: $210k/yr (blended).

Scenario matrix (short descriptions)
- BASELINE: no region price shocks, procurement cadence as planned, small priority hiring in infra early.
- H100-EMEA SQUEEZE: H100 spot/pool prices +45% in EMEA for Q1-Q2, forcing more burst to US or degraded throughput for EMEA customers.
- AGGRESSIVE_GTM: pricing acceptable => token volume +2.8x, requires earlier hiring and more dedicated capacity to keep latency.
- PRICE_SHOCK_CONSERVATIVE: cloud GPU prices up +60% globally for three months (supply shock) -> evaluate drawdown options and temporary price increases.

Short-run model outputs (9-month aggregated view, note rough numbers)
- Baseline: tokens served = 120B tokens, infra cost = $2.88M, personnel incremental cost = $1.26M (8 FTEs * 210k * 9/12), gross margin (pre-opex) ~ 63%.
- H100-EMEA Squeeze: infra cost delta = +$0.42M (14.6% increase) if we absorb region price; if we shift traffic -> extra egress/buffer cost +$0.28M and 4% latency SLA breaches risk. Net margin drops ~4-6 ppts.
- Aggressive_GTM: tokens=336B, infra cost scaling non-linear due to queuing and ops inefficiency if we don't add capacity. If we add 18 FTEs immediately and reserve 30% extra capacity, net margin target maintained but incremental opex ~ $3.15M (blended 18 * 210k * 9/12).
- Price_Shock_Conservative: short 3-month burst +60% -> immediate cash impact +$1.1M on infra; mitigations: temporary 10% price pass-through -> revenue elasticity assumed -6% (churn + lower usage), net outcome: margin compression ~7-12 ppts in shock window.

Headcount phasing (proposal)
- Q1: hire 3 infra (priority), 1 SRE, 1 solutions engineer (focus EMEA GTM).
- Q2: hire 2 backend SWE, 1 product reliability program manager, 1 CSE.
- Hiring triggers: scale infra hiring sooner if observed throughput > +40% above baseline over 2 consecutive weeks or EMEA H100 spot index > +30% and sustained.

Pricing playbook levers tested
1) Temporary price pass-through (short windows, targeted regions) — quick to implement but hurts usage elasticity.
2) Commit tiers for Dedicated / Reserved capacity (discounts in exchange for term) — protects margin if customers accept.
3) Model routing to cheaper variants (lighter quantized models for non-latency-critical) — preserves UX if executed cleanly.
4) Cache and batch incentives (rebates for customers who tolerate slightly higher latency) — product-ops/CS required.

Simple sensitivity table (selected slices, nine-month cumulative)
- If per-token infra cost +10% -> margin -2.3 ppts.
- If per-token infra cost +30% -> margin -6.9 ppts.
- If revenue per token -10% (price promo) -> margin -8.3 ppts.
- If tokens +50% without hiring/additional reserved -> margin -9.8 ppts (due to inefficient burst mix).

Risk notes and operational constraints
- Dedicated procurement lead times for H100-class hardware ~12-18 weeks; reserving earlier helps but locks capital.
- Egress, cross-region costs and multi-cloud redundancy can materially increase effective per-token cost if traffic shifts.
- Sales incentives tied to consumption can exacerbate short-term bursts; consider gating or smoothing credits.

Open questions / items for follow-up
- Obtain updated spot/commit price curves from partners for US, EMEA, APAC (ask infra procurement to pull latest quotes by 2026-02-20).
- Validate revenue elasticity against actual embedded customers (work with CS to segment customers by price sensitivity).
- Model a hybrid reserve-buyback option: buy reserved capacity now with residual credits for cloud burst. Need legal review.

Quick next steps (owners / dates)
- Procurement: fetch region-tiered quotes and H100 allocation timelines (owner: Jonah Kim, due 2026-02-20).
- Product: define model-routing priority rules for quantized variants (owner: Priya Nair, due 2026-02-28).
- Finance: bake these scenarios into the rolling 18m runway model and produce delta waterfall (owner: Aisha Patel, due 2026-03-05).

Appendix (back-of-envelope math lines)
- Baseline infra cost math: 120B tokens * $0.000024 = $2.88M.
- Incremental FTE cost: 8 * $210k * 0.75 = $1.26M.
- Price shock: assume 3-month exposure to 60% uplift on 40% of traffic -> delta tokens cost = (120B * 0.4 * 0.25) * 0.000024 * 0.6 ≈ $1.15M.

Notes to reviewers
- This is an exploratory sheet; numbers are intentionally rounded and assumptions call out where we must validate. Please flag obvious model omissions or preferred mitigation levers you want explored.
- Prefer short sync with infra procurement and product ops to align assumptions.

Document history
- 2026-01-05: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2026-01-20: added scenarios and HC phasing (Jonah)
- 2026-02-15: updated with EMEA H100 squeeze sensitivity and revised math (Priya)
